texts: F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote "The Sound and the Fury" in the late 1920s, publishing it in 1929. His exploration of the decline of the Southern aristocracy, along with his distinctive lyrical prose, complemented the poignant themes of time and memory. This novel marked a defining moment in Fitzgerald's literary career, solidifying his reputation as a groundbreaking modernist author.
F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote "The Sound and the Fury" in 1924. The novel was published by Charles Scribner's Sons.

F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote "The Sound and the Fury" between 1928 and 1930. It is one of the novels in the collection of four novels and one long short story known as "The Cannes Stories," which Fitzgerald was working on during these years. Despite several revisions, the novel was not published until 1940, four years after Fitzgerald's death.

F. Scott Fitzgerald did not write "The Sound and the Fury". The novel "The Sound and the Fury" was actually written by William Faulkner and was first published in 1929. It is considered one of Faulkner's most important works and is known for its non-linear narrative structure and complex themes.

F. Scott Fitzgerald, on the other hand, was a different American author, known for his novels and short stories that often explored the Jazz Age and the American Dream. Some of his most famous works include "The Great Gatsby", "Tender Is the Night", and "The Diamond as Big as the Ritz".
